subject: Follow-up: latency & qps profile — hosted vs dedicated deployment options
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@edgecommerce.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: latency & qps profile — hosted vs dedicated deployment options

Hi Jordan — great chat today, thanks for walking through the EdgeCommerce use case. Quick recap + a few clarifying questions so we can size a concrete recommendation between Hosted API and Dedicated capacity.

Recap of what you shared (please correct anything I got wrong):
- Current traffic: ~500 RPS (requests/sec) steady state; peak bursts up to ~1.6k RPS during promo windows.
- Target p95 inference latency: <= 220 ms for customer-facing flows.
- Model: a 13B encoder-decoder used for short text completion and reranking. Typical prompt lengths are 60–120 tokens, responses 20–60 tokens.
- Data residency: no strict legal residency today; may need VPC access for PCI card-scrubbing flow later.
- Timeline: pilot in September, production H2 2027.

Clarifying questions we need to validate before we benchmark:
1) Are the 1.6k RPS spikes sustained for multiple minutes or are they short 1–2 minute bursts?
2) Do you have a sample of the production request payloads (anonymized) and token-length distribution?
3) Any hard throughput SLA for the promos window or is availability + best-effort OK?

My high-level recommendation options (so you and Priya can weigh):
- Hosted API: fastest path to pilot; we can run an optimized hosted profile with KV caching + continuous batching. Usually the simplest for teams that need speed to market. Latency at scale can be competitive but depends on burst shaping and prefix reuse.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pool (V100/A100 class) for predictable p95 and throughput; better for sustained high QPS and strict latency SLOs. Also supports pinning model variants and private network peering.

Proposed next steps:
- You share a 5–10 minute sample of traffic + token distribution (CSV).
- We run a targeted benchmark on both Hosted (optimized runtime) and a Dedicated baseline that matches your peak profile. We’ll return p50/p95/p99 and cost-per-1M-token estimates.
- 30-minute technical deep dive with Markus to validate caching/quantization tradeoffs.

I’ve attached a short decision matrix (redwood-deploy-mode-quick-matrix.xlsx) and a checklist for the technical call. If you’re good, I can schedule the benchmark and carve out time for the deep dive next week.

Thanks — Mina

--
Mina Haddad
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0134
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@edgecommerce.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Nair <priya.nair@edgecommerce.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: latency & qps profile — hosted vs dedicated deployment options

Mina — thanks for the clear recap. Couple quick answers:
- The 1.6k RPS bursts typically last 3–7 minutes and occur a few times during promotional events. They’re predictable (we know windows) but we can’t drop requests there — must remain available.
- I’ll send an anonymized sample payload + token distribution by EOD today (Priya is pulling).
- No hard SLA in contracts today, but the product team needs p95 <= 220ms at those peaks or we will need to rethink UX (timeouts, queuing).

Cost sensitivity: we’re mindful of OpEx — if Hosted meets the p95 target during peaks we’d prefer that to avoid a heavy committed contract. However, we’re open to Hybrid approaches if you can show a clear breakeven.

Can you also provide a ballpark SLA (uptime / credits) for Dedicated vs Hosted? We need that for procurement.

Available for the deep dive: Thu 09:00–11:00 PT or Fri 13:00–16:00 PT.

—Jordan
VP Product, EdgeCommerce
jordan.lee@edgecommerce.com

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@edgecommerce.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 15:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: latency & qps profile — hosted vs dedicated deployment options

Great — thanks Jordan, that timeline works. Priya, appreciate you pulling the sample payloads.

Quick answers up front so procurement has something to work with:
- Hosted API: standard uptime SLA is 99.9% for paid tiers; credits and dedicated routing options available for larger commitments.
- Dedicated: can be part of a reserved capacity agreement with 99.95% SLA and options for additional support/response SLAs as part of an enterprise contract. I’ll surface standard wording; final SLA depends on committed capacity and support tier.

Technical intuition (non-binding):
- For the model size and short prompts you described, Dedicated capacity configured with single-request pre-warming and minimal batching will almost always give the most consistent p95 under sustained load.
- Hosted with smart batching and KV prefix caching can often reach p95 targets for short bursts, but sustained high bursts (multiple minutes at 1.6k RPS) typically benefit from Dedicated to avoid queuing/backpressure if you need strict p95.

Markus — can you prepare a short runbook we can share with Jordan that lists: recommended reserved GPU count for a 1.6k peak, expected p95 ranges for Hosted vs Dedicated (ballpark), and the pieces we’ll need from EdgeCommerce to run the benchmark? I attached a precall checklist with the things we’ll ask them to upload.

I’ll go ahead and schedule the 30-minute deep dive for Thu 09:30 PT and send a calendar invite with a short agenda. If that time doesn’t work please flag.

Thanks — Mina

--
Mina Haddad
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@edgecommerce.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 17:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: latency & qps profile — hosted vs dedicated deployment options

Jordan / team — Markus here from Inference Engineering. Short technical notes ahead of the deep dive and the benchmark.

What I’ll bring to the call:
- A rough sizing spreadsheet (reserved GPU count estimate) for a 1.6k RPS sustained burst at the token lengths you mentioned.
- Expected p95 ranges: Dedicated (single-request path, warm KV cache) ~120–200 ms depending on model quantization and batch-concurrency; Hosted (optimized runtime, continuous batching) ~180–300 ms depending on burst shaping and prefix reuse. These are empirical ranges — the benchmark will give precise numbers.
- Tradeoffs to discuss: batching vs latency, quantization quality vs latency/cost, prefix/KV caching opportunities, and fallback policies (e.g., route to lower-latency model variant during peaks).

What we need from you for the benchmark:
1) Anonymized sample payloads (CSV) and token-length distribution.
2) A short list of representative endpoints (customer-facing vs internal) so we can weight the traffic mix.
3) Any network constraints (e.g., VPC peering required, egress limits).

Post-call deliverables: benchmark report (p50/p95/p99 + cost estimate), a one-page recommendation (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Hybrid) and a proposed pilot timeline.

I’ll upload the sizing doc to the Drive folder linked in the from thread and bring the spreadsheet to the call. See you Thu 09:30 PT.

—Markus
Senior Director, Inference Engineering
Redwood Inference
